newsitem.title: FRANCE: Giscard says French deficit key to EMU -paper.
newsitem.headline: Giscard says French deficit key to EMU -paper.

text.p: The new French government's attempts to curb public deficits is the key to the success of European economic and monetary union (EMU), said former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing said on Friday in a newspaper interview.
He also said a failure to launch a single currency would be very dangerous for France.

He told afternoon daily Le Monde ratification of the so-called stability and growth pact at an Amsterdam summit earlier this year had removed the last remaining political obstacle to the successful launch of a single currency.
"Only one obstacle remains, that of budget deficits. That's why France holds the key to the system. If France resolves its deficit problem, we will have monetary union," he was quoted as saying.
"Germany, in my opinion, will deal with its problem. I hope that France is going to take the decisions compatible with this (deficit cutting) objective," he said.
